ledger.note: 296: the Yang Di state of Chouchi. Infobox 'Established: 296' and 'Former Chouchi lasted between 296 and 371'; the Yang Maosou page has Maosou succeed his father in 296 and lead 'around 4,000 families to resettle in Chouchi' in c. January 297. The page gives the mountain, not a boundary.

region.text: Hanzhong, briefly controlled by Yang Nandi 313-314

ledger.note: 313: Yang Nandi takes Hanzhong from Jin's Inspector of Liang. 'In 313, Jin's Inspector of Liang, Zhang Guang, campaigned against the refugee rebel leader, Yang Hu'; Nandi, sent to aid Jin, switched sides, and 'defeated Zhang Guang and briefly controlled Hanzhong'. The page dates the campaign to 313 and the ousting to 314; the year of the conquest is the researcher's.

region.text: Hanzhong, briefly controlled by Yang Nandi 313-314

ledger.note: 314: Hanzhong is lost. Nandi was 'ousted back to Chouchi by a local revolt in 314'.

region.text: Mount Chouchi in present-day Longnan, Gansu (the page: the Di 'migrate to Mount Chouchi'); drawn as a 90 km disc, the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 371: Former Qin ends the Former Chouchi. Qin 'attacked Chouchi, captured the ruler Yang Cuan (楊篡) and ended the period of Former Chouchi' (Chouchi page); the Former Qin page: 'In 371, Qin conquered Chouchi.'

region.text: Mount Chouchi in present-day Longnan, Gansu (the page: the Di 'migrate to Mount Chouchi'); drawn as a 90 km disc, the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 385: Yang Ding resurrects Chouchi. He 'resurrected the Chouchi kingdom in 385, with the capital at Licheng'; the Yang Ding page: he 'proclaimed himself as Prancing Dragon General and Duke of Chouchi in 385', after Former Qin's collapse. The year is the page's, the land is the old core.

region.text: Longcheng and Jicheng in Tianshui, taken in 389

ledger.note: 389: Yang Ding takes Longcheng and Jicheng. 'He took Longcheng and Jicheng in Tianshui in 389, and in the same year declared himself Prince of Longxi'; he beat Yao Chang and Xing Nu of Later Qin.

region.text: Longcheng and Jicheng in Tianshui, taken in 389

ledger.note: 394: Yang Ding is killed; Tianshui goes. Yang Ding fought Qifu Gangui at Pingchuan and 'was overwhelmed in a counterattack'; his cousin Yang Sheng succeeded him only as Duke of Chouchi. The page does not say who took Tianshui; Western Qin took Longxi in 394 (western-qin dossier). Confidence 1: the loss is inferred.

region.text: Chouchi round Mount Chouchi with Wudu, for Later Chouchi; the page says only that the Yang 'controlled a large part of the modern provinces of Gansu (east) and Shaanxi (south)', no year

ledger.note: 442: Liu Song conquers Chouchi. Infobox 'Conquered by Liu Song: 442'; the ruler list ends Yang Baochi 442-443. The page narrates nothing.

region.text: the Kingdom of Wudu (Wudu District, Longnan, Gansu): 'Kings of Wudu (443-477)'

ledger.note: 443: Northern Wei conquers Chouchi and Yang Wende restores it the same year. 'In 443, the Northern Wei conquered Chouchi, but was restored by Yang Wende that same year'; 'After 443, the lords of Chouchi were only puppet rulers controlled by the Northern and Southern dynasties.' The infobox says restored as Wudu, Wuxing and Yinping in 448.
443: the Kingdom of Wudu. The ruler table lists 'Kings of Wudu (443-477)' under Yang Wende (443-454); the infobox dates the restoration as Wudu, Wuxing and Yinping to 448.

477: Chouchi splits in two. 'After the death of Yang Wendu in 477, the realm split into Yinping and Wuxing.' Wendu had attacked Wei in 473 and again in 477; 'his head was sent to Pingcheng' and Wei installed Yang Guangxiang as Duke of Yinping while his brother Yang Wenhong inherited Wuxing (Yang Wendu page). Both branches stay in this dossier.

ledger.note: 506: Wuxing drops out. The ruler table gives Yang Shaoxian 503-506 and again 534-535, with no king of Wuxing between; the Northern Wei page opened is silent (it has only Xinyang and Hanzhong falling in spring 505). Confidence 1: a gap in the table.

region.text: Wuxing, 'present-day Lueyang County, Shaanxi' (Yang Wendu page)

ledger.note: 534: Wuxing returns. Yang Shaoxian reigns again 534-535 (page table); no sentence gives the event. Confidence 1.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (slug chouchi, as ea-03-b/c asked). One dossier for the Yang house's mountain kingdom from 296 to 580: Former Chouchi 296-371, Later Chouchi 385-442, the Wudu puppet kingdom 443-476, then the Wuxing and Yinping branches in parallel to 552 and 580. The Chouchi page gives no area or boundary; every shape is a disc round a modern seat, so the whole life is soft. Not found on the pages opened: the Cheng-Han vassalage date, the Later Qin vassalage of 405 (carried in the later-qin dossier, counterpart chouchi), any conquest by Yang Sheng or Nandang (the page's 'large part of eastern Gansu and southern Shaanxi' is undated), the Liu Song campaign of 442, the 506 and 534 Wuxing dates (table gaps, confidence 1), Hanzhong after 314. Disagreement: the Chouchi page dates the Wudu restoration 443 in the text and 448 in the infobox; 296 (Chouchi infobox) against c. January 297 (Yang Maosou page). Places the gazetteer lacks (discs were used instead): Mount Chouchi / Longnan, Wudu, Lueyang, Wen County, Licheng, Xinghe, Fanshi. Counterpart slugs used without a dossier of their own in this batch: none; western-qin, later-qin, former-qin, liu-song-dynasty, northern-wei, western-wei, northern-zhou, former-zhao, western-yan exist. Matching events other dossiers should carry: former-qin gain 371 (present), later-qin vassal 405 (present) and a loss of Tianshui 389, western-qin gain of Tianshui 394, liu-song-dynasty gain 442, northern-wei gain 443, western-wei gain 552, northern-zhou gain 580.
